title: The King's Happy Plan
captions: Everyone in Ayodhya loved Prince Rama. He was always calm and gentle, and he was the first to greet people with a kind word. He remembered every kindness done to him and soon forgot any wrong.
King Dasharatha had grown old. He thought, “Rama is wise and good, and the people love him. Let him become the yuvaraja, the crown prince, and help me rule.”
The king called a great assembly of princes, ministers and people from the city and the villages. When he shared his plan, they all cheered with one voice: “Let Rama be our crown prince!”

The king asked Vasishtha to prepare the ceremony for the next morning. Sumantra brought Rama, who bowed at his father's feet. “Tomorrow you will be crowned,” said the king. “Always stay humble and gentle.”

Rama went to his mother. Queen Kausalya was already praying for him, with Sumitra, Lakshmana and Sita beside her. “Lakshmana,” said Rama, “you are like my own self. We will care for this kingdom together.”
That evening Vasishtha came to Rama's palace and asked Rama and Sita to keep a fast. They prayed to Lord Narayana, made offerings into the sacred fire and slept on a bed of kusha grass.
All night the people made Ayodhya beautiful. They raised flags, sprinkled the streets and lit rows of lamps. Everyone waited happily for the morning when Rama would be crowned.
story: Everyone in Ayodhya loved Prince Rama. He was always calm and spoke gently. He was the first to greet others with a kind word. If someone did him one kindness, he remembered it forever, and if someone wronged him, he soon forgot it.

King Dasharatha had grown old. He saw how wise and good Rama was and how much the people loved him. He decided that Rama should become the yuvaraja, the crown prince, and share the work of ruling the kingdom.

The king called a great assembly of princes, ministers and people from the city and the villages. He told them his plan. With one voice they cheered and praised Rama's goodness, his courage and his kindness to all.

The king asked his gurus Vasishtha and Vamadeva to prepare the ceremony for the next morning. His minister Sumantra brought Rama to the court in a chariot. Rama bowed at his father's feet, and the king lifted him up and embraced him. He told Rama he would be crowned the next day and advised him to stay humble and gentle always.

Rama hurried to tell his mother. Queen Kausalya was already praying for him, with Queen Sumitra, Lakshmana and Sita beside her. Rama told Lakshmana that he was like his own self and that they would care for the kingdom together. That evening Vasishtha asked Rama and Sita to keep a fast. They prayed to Lord Narayana and slept on kusha grass, while the people lit lamps all over Ayodhya and waited happily for the morning.
lesson: The people of Ayodhya did not love Rama only because he was a prince. They loved him because he was kind to everyone, greeted people first, remembered every kindness and forgave quickly. In our tradition, Sadachara means good conduct, the way we behave each day. Our elders teach that good conduct wins hearts more surely than power or riches, and Rama's gentle ways won the heart of a whole city.
lesson_long: Sadachara means good conduct: being kind, honest and respectful in the small things we do every day.

Rama was a prince, but he never acted proud. He greeted people first, spoke gently, remembered every kindness and quickly forgot any wrong. When the king asked the people what they thought, the whole city cheered for Rama because of the way he treated them.
Our elders teach that good conduct wins hearts more surely than power or riches.
tradition: Lord Rama is often called Maryada Purushottama, which means the best of people, who always keeps to what is right and proper. Many families tell Rama's stories to their children so they can learn good conduct from him, and his kind, fair rule is remembered as Ram Rajya.

Before a holy day, many Hindus keep a vrata, a fast or vow, and pray with a quiet mind, just as Rama and Sita did that night. On Rama Navami, the day of Rama's birth, many devotees fast, sing his name and read the Ramayana.

a sacred fast or vow kept with prayer
a sacred grass used in prayers
question: What is one kind thing you can do that would make someone happy today?
